details: The upcoming June US Consumer Price Index (CPI) report, scheduled for July 14, is a critical event for financial markets. The Federal Reserve, under Chair Kevin Warsh, continues to signal a hawkish stance, with a majority of FOMC officials projecting at least one rate hike in 2026. Persistently high inflation readings could lead to the Fed maintaining elevated interest rates or implementing further hikes, which typically increases the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding assets like Bitcoin and can lead to money rotating out of speculative assets. While energy inflation appears to be fading, concerns are emerging about potential inflationary pressures from AI-related demand.
title: US CPI Looms: Fed's Hawkish Stance Pressures Crypto

details: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has lowered its 2026 global growth projection to 3.0%, a reduction from its April forecast of 3.1%. This downgrade is primarily attributed to the lingering effects of the Middle East energy shock and a projected rise in global headline inflation to 4.7% for 2026. The slowdown is partially offset by an accelerated demand-driven momentum in the global technology cycle, particularly due to advances in artificial intelligence. Ongoing geopolitical tensions, especially the US-Iran conflict, are contributing to oil price volatility and broader economic uncertainty, fostering a risk-off sentiment in financial markets.
title: IMF Cuts 2026 Global Growth Forecast Amid Mideast War & Inflation

details: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has issued a warning regarding the potential systemic risks posed by USD-pegged stablecoins during periods of financial crises. The IMF report highlights that while stablecoins can improve foreign exchange accessibility, they could also facilitate "bank run"-like scenarios by enabling massive transfers of funds from local currencies to USD assets. Such rapid shifts could exacerbate financial instability and trigger widespread USD shortages, impacting the broader financial system.
title: IMF Flags 'Bank Run' Risks from USD Stablecoins in Crises

details: Long-term Bitcoin holders have resumed accumulation, adding a net 5,912 BTC on July 11-12. This pattern of accumulation by patient investors was last observed just before a 25% rally in February. Concurrently, US spot Bitcoin Exchange-Traded Funds (ETFs) have experienced their first week of net inflows in eight weeks, attracting $197 million in the week ending July 10. These developments suggest a potential shift in market sentiment and renewed confidence from significant market participants in the leading cryptocurrency.
title: Bitcoin Long-Term Holders Accumulate, ETFs End Outflow Streak
